age_at_death.question: Who lived longer?
age_at_death.definition_note: Age in whole years at death, from recorded birth and death dates. Ancient ages are best estimates.
age_at_death.fact_default: The longest verified human lifespan is 122 years, reached by Jeanne Calment.

airport_passengers.question: Which airport is busier?
airport_passengers.definition_note: Passengers boarding at the airport in 2024 (enplanements), from the FAA.
airport_passengers.fact_default: Atlanta has been the world's busiest airport by passengers almost every year since 1998.

animal_gestation.subject: animal
animal_gestation.question: Which animal is pregnant longer?
animal_gestation.question_low: Which animal has the shorter pregnancy?
animal_gestation.definition_note: Typical gestation length in days. Sources: AnAge (Human Ageing Genomic Resources) and PanTHERIA.
animal_gestation.fact_default: Elephants are pregnant for about 22 months, the longest of any land animal.

animal_max_lifespan.subject: animal
animal_max_lifespan.question: Which animal can live longer?
animal_max_lifespan.question_low: Which animal has the shorter maximum lifespan?
animal_max_lifespan.definition_note: Longest recorded lifespan for the species, in years. Sources: AnAge (Human Ageing Genomic Resources) and PanTHERIA.
animal_max_lifespan.fact_default: Bowhead whales can live over 200 years, the longest of any mammal.

animal_weight.subject: animal
animal_weight.question: Which animal is heavier?
animal_weight.definition_note: Typical adult body mass in kilograms, from the AnAge and PanTHERIA species databases. Sources: AnAge (Human Ageing Genomic Resources) and PanTHERIA.
animal_weight.fact_default: A blue whale's heart alone weighs about as much as a small car.

broadway_performances.question: Which Broadway show ran for more performances?
broadway_performances.question_low: Which Broadway show had fewer performances?
broadway_performances.definition_note: Regular performances of the original Broadway run (previews excluded) as of September 27, 2026, from Playbill, checked against Wikipedia. Totals for shows still running keep growing.
broadway_performances.fact_default: The Phantom of the Opera played 13,981 performances over 35 years, the longest run in Broadway history.

building_height.question: Which building is taller?
building_height.scope_note: Height to architectural top, antennas excluded
building_height.definition_note: Height to architectural top (CTBUH standard): spires count, antennas and flagpoles do not.
building_height.fact_default: From the top of Burj Khalifa you can watch the sun set a few minutes after it has set at ground level.

city_annual_precipitation.subject: us_city
city_annual_precipitation.question: Which city gets more rain each year?
city_annual_precipitation.question_low: Which city gets less rain each year?
city_annual_precipitation.definition_note: Average yearly precipitation (rain plus melted snow) in inches. Annual normal for 1991–2020 at the city's main weather station (usually its airport), from NOAA, checked against Wikipedia's climate table.
city_annual_precipitation.fact_default: Hilo, Hawaii averages about 120 inches of rain a year, wetter than any big mainland US city.

city_annual_snowfall.subject: us_city
city_annual_snowfall.question: Which city gets more snow each year?
city_annual_snowfall.question_low: Which city gets less snow each year?
city_annual_snowfall.definition_note: Average yearly snowfall in inches. Annual normal for 1991–2020 at the city's main weather station (usually its airport), from NOAA, checked against Wikipedia's climate table.
city_annual_snowfall.fact_default: Syracuse, New York averages over 120 inches of snow a year, more than any other big US city.

coaster_height.subject: coaster
coaster_height.question: Which roller coaster is taller?
coaster_height.definition_note: Height of the coaster's highest point in feet. From the Roller Coaster DataBase (RCDB), checked against Wikipedia.
coaster_height.fact_default: Kingda Ka in New Jersey was the world's tallest coaster at 456 feet until it closed in 2024.

coaster_speed.subject: coaster
coaster_speed.question: Which roller coaster is faster?
coaster_speed.definition_note: Top speed in miles per hour. From the Roller Coaster DataBase (RCDB), checked against Wikipedia.
coaster_speed.fact_default: Formula Rossa in Abu Dhabi launches riders to 149 mph in under 5 seconds.

college_undergrads.question: Which college has more undergraduates?
college_undergrads.definition_note: Degree-seeking undergraduates enrolled in fall 2022 at the main campus, from federal IPEDS data (Urban Institute Education Data Portal and College Scorecard).
college_undergrads.fact_default: Texas A&M has more undergraduates than any other US campus, over 50,000.

company_founded.subject: company
company_founded.question: Which company was founded first?
company_founded.question_low: Which company was founded more recently?
company_founded.definition_note: Year the company, or the direct predecessor its founders started, was founded.
company_founded.fact_default: Japan's Kongō Gumi, founded in 578, ran for more than 1,400 years.

company_revenue_2023.subject: company
company_revenue_2023.question: Which company had more revenue in fiscal 2023?
company_revenue_2023.question_low: Which company had less revenue in fiscal 2023?
company_revenue_2023.scope_note: Fiscal 2023, as each company labels it
company_revenue_2023.definition_note: Total revenue for fiscal year 2023 as each company labels it, in US dollars, from annual reports.
company_revenue_2023.fact_default: Walmart employs about 2.1 million people worldwide.

country_area.subject: country
country_area.question: Which country is bigger?
country_area.scope_note: Total area, land and inland water
country_area.definition_note: Total area (land plus inland water) in square kilometres. Sources differ by up to a few percent, so close pairs are never used.
country_area.fact_default: Russia covers about one-ninth of Earth's land.

country_coastline.subject: country
country_coastline.question: Which country has more coastline?
country_coastline.definition_note: Total length of coastline as listed by the CIA World Factbook. Coastline length depends on how finely it is measured.
country_coastline.fact_default: Canada has the longest coastline in the world, more than 200,000 km including its islands.

country_gdp.subject: country
country_gdp.question: Which country has the bigger economy?
country_gdp.question_low: Which country has the smaller economy?
country_gdp.definition_note: Gross domestic product in 2024, current US dollars (World Bank). Not adjusted for purchasing power.
country_gdp.fact_default: The US and China together make up about 40% of the world economy.

country_land_neighbors.subject: country
country_land_neighbors.question: Which country borders more countries?
country_land_neighbors.definition_note: Number of countries sharing a land border, from the CIA World Factbook, checked against Wikipedia.
country_land_neighbors.fact_default: China and Russia each border 14 countries, more than any others.

country_life_expectancy.subject: country
country_life_expectancy.question: In which country do people live longer?
country_life_expectancy.question_low: In which country is life expectancy lower?
country_life_expectancy.definition_note: Life expectancy at birth in 2021, both sexes, from the World Bank (UN estimates), checked against the WHO Global Health Observatory.
country_life_expectancy.fact_default: Japan has had one of the world's highest life expectancies for decades, around 84 years.

country_population.subject: country
country_population.question: Which country has more people?
country_population.definition_note: Mid-2024 population estimates from the UN World Population Prospects 2024.
country_population.fact_default: The world's population passed 8 billion in November 2022.

element_atomic_weight.subject: element
element_atomic_weight.question: Which element has the heavier atoms?
element_atomic_weight.question_low: Which element has the lighter atoms?
element_atomic_weight.definition_note: Standard atomic weight (IUPAC), in daltons. For radioactive elements, the mass number of the longest-lived isotope.
element_atomic_weight.fact_default: Atomic weight is roughly the number of protons plus neutrons.

element_discovered.subject: element
element_discovered.question: Which element was discovered first?
element_discovered.question_low: Which element was discovered more recently?
element_discovered.definition_note: Year the element was first isolated or identified as an element. Elements known since ancient times are left out.
element_discovered.fact_default: Hennig Brand discovered phosphorus in 1669 while boiling down urine, looking for gold.

element_melting_point.subject: element
element_melting_point.question: Which element has the higher melting point?
element_melting_point.question_low: Which element has the lower melting point?
element_melting_point.definition_note: Melting point at standard pressure in degrees Celsius. Gaps are measured in kelvin.
element_melting_point.fact_default: Carbon doesn't melt at normal pressure; it turns straight into gas.

film_release_year.subject: film
film_release_year.question: Which movie came out first?
film_release_year.question_low: Which movie came out more recently?
film_release_year.definition_note: Year of first theatrical release in the film's home country.
film_release_year.fact_default: The first feature-length talkie, The Jazz Singer, came out in 1927.

film_runtime.subject: film
film_runtime.question: Which movie is longer?
film_runtime.definition_note: Running time of the original theatrical release in minutes. Extended and director's cuts excluded.
film_runtime.fact_default: With its overture and intermission, Gone with the Wind runs nearly four hours.

film_worldwide_gross.subject: film
film_worldwide_gross.question: Which movie made more at the worldwide box office?
film_worldwide_gross.question_low: Which movie made less at the worldwide box office?
film_worldwide_gross.definition_note: Lifetime worldwide gross in US dollars, re-releases included, not adjusted for inflation.
film_worldwide_gross.fact_default: Box office totals here are not adjusted for inflation.

food_calories.question: Which has more calories per 100 grams?
food_calories.question_low: Which has fewer calories per 100 grams?
food_calories.definition_note: Food energy per 100 g of the edible part, from USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy).
food_calories.fact_default: Fat has more than twice the calories per gram of protein or carbohydrate.

food_protein.question: Gram for gram, which has more protein?
food_protein.question_low: Gram for gram, which has less protein?
food_protein.definition_note: Protein in grams. Per 100 grams, from USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy), checked against NutritionValue.org.
food_protein.fact_default: Gram for gram, grated parmesan has more protein than roast chicken breast.

food_sugar_per_100g.question: Gram for gram, which has more sugar?
food_sugar_per_100g.question_low: Gram for gram, which has less sugar?
food_sugar_per_100g.definition_note: Total sugars in grams. Per 100 grams, from USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy), checked against NutritionValue.org.
food_sugar_per_100g.fact_default: Gram for gram, a mango has more sugar than a banana, and grapes beat both.

food_vitamin_c.question: Gram for gram, which has more vitamin C?
food_vitamin_c.question_low: Gram for gram, which has less vitamin C?
food_vitamin_c.definition_note: Vitamin C in milligrams. Per 100 grams, from USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy), checked against NutritionValue.org.
food_vitamin_c.fact_default: Gram for gram, a guava or a red bell pepper has more vitamin C than an orange.

grammy_wins.question: Who has won more Grammys?
grammy_wins.definition_note: Career Grammy Awards won, as counted by the Recording Academy, through the 2025 ceremony.
grammy_wins.fact_default: Beyoncé holds the record for the most Grammy wins of any artist.

historical_event_year.question: Which happened first?
historical_event_year.definition_note: Year the event happened, or began for events spanning several years.
historical_event_year.fact_default: Oxford University was already teaching before the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan was founded.

hot100_weeks_at_no1.subject: song
hot100_weeks_at_no1.question: Which song spent more weeks at No. 1?
hot100_weeks_at_no1.question_low: Which song spent fewer weeks at No. 1?
hot100_weeks_at_no1.definition_note: Total weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, all runs combined.
hot100_weeks_at_no1.fact_default: Only about 4% of all Hot 100 No. 1 songs have stayed on top for 10 weeks or more.

landmark_completed.subject: landmark
landmark_completed.question: Which was completed first?
landmark_completed.definition_note: Year construction was completed (or the landmark opened). Ancient dates are scholarly estimates.
landmark_completed.fact_default: The Great Pyramid was already over 2,000 years old when the Parthenon was built.

landmark_height.subject: landmark
landmark_height.question: Which landmark is taller?
landmark_height.scope_note: Ground to highest point, pedestal included
landmark_height.definition_note: Total height from ground (or water for bridges) to the highest point, including pedestals and antennas.
landmark_height.fact_default: The Eiffel Tower was the tallest structure in the world for 41 years.

lego_set_pieces.question: Which LEGO set has more pieces?
lego_set_pieces.question_low: Which LEGO set has fewer pieces?
lego_set_pieces.definition_note: Piece count of the set as listed by Brickset, checked against Rebrickable's parts inventory.
lego_set_pieces.fact_default: The 2022 LEGO Eiffel Tower has 10,001 pieces and stands almost 5 feet tall.

mlb_career_hr.question: Who hit more career home runs?
mlb_career_hr.question_low: Who hit fewer career home runs?
mlb_career_hr.definition_note: Career home runs in MLB regular-season games. Postseason excluded. Retired players only, so totals are final.
mlb_career_hr.fact_default: Only four players have hit 700 or more MLB home runs.

monarch_reign.question: Which monarch reigned longer?
monarch_reign.question_low: Which monarch had the shorter reign?
monarch_reign.definition_note: Length of reign as monarch of England (from 1066) or of Great Britain and the United Kingdom.
monarch_reign.fact_default: Elizabeth II reigned for 70 years, the longest of any British monarch.

mountain_elevation.question: Which mountain is higher?
mountain_elevation.definition_note: Summit elevation above sea level in metres.
mountain_elevation.fact_default: Elevation is measured from sea level, not from the mountain's base.

national_park_area.question: Which national park is bigger?
national_park_area.definition_note: Gross area within the park boundary, in acres, from the National Park Service land resources report.
national_park_area.fact_default: Wrangell–St. Elias, the biggest US national park, is larger than Switzerland.

nba_career_fg_pct.subject: nba
nba_career_fg_pct.question: Who had the higher career field goal percentage?
nba_career_fg_pct.question_low: Who had the lower career field goal percentage?
nba_career_fg_pct.definition_note: Career field goal percentage in NBA regular-season games. Retired players only.
nba_career_fg_pct.fact_default: Wilt Chamberlain once made 35 field goals in a row, spread over several games in 1967.

nba_career_points.subject: nba
nba_career_points.question: Who scored more career NBA points?
nba_career_points.question_low: Who scored fewer career NBA points?
nba_career_points.definition_note: Career points in NBA regular-season games. Playoffs and ABA excluded. Retired players only.
nba_career_points.fact_default: LeBron James became the first player to pass 40,000 regular-season points in 2024.

nfl_career_pass_td.question: Who threw more career touchdown passes?
nfl_career_pass_td.question_low: Who threw fewer career touchdown passes?
nfl_career_pass_td.definition_note: Regular-season NFL career passing touchdowns. Retired players only.
nfl_career_pass_td.fact_default: Tom Brady threw 649 regular-season touchdown passes, plus 88 more in the playoffs.

olympic_golds.question: Who won more Olympic gold medals?
olympic_golds.question_low: Who won fewer Olympic gold medals?
olympic_golds.definition_note: Career Olympic gold medals, Summer and Winter Games combined. Retired athletes only.
olympic_golds.fact_default: Olympic gold medals have been mostly silver, plated with gold, since 1912.

oscar_wins.subject: film
oscar_wins.question: Which movie won more Oscars?
oscar_wins.definition_note: Competitive Academy Awards won by the film. Honorary and special awards are not counted.
oscar_wins.fact_default: Three films share the record of 11 Oscars: Ben-Hur, Titanic and The Return of the King.

pokemon_weight.question: Which Pokémon is heavier?
pokemon_weight.definition_note: Official weight in kilograms as listed in the Pokédex, from PokéAPI and Pokémon Showdown.
pokemon_weight.fact_default: Snorlax weighs 460 kg in the Pokédex, more than a grand piano.

president_inauguration_age.question: Which president was older at their first inauguration?
president_inauguration_age.question_low: Which president was younger at their first inauguration?
president_inauguration_age.definition_note: Age in whole years on the day of the president's first inauguration.
president_inauguration_age.fact_default: The Constitution requires presidents to be at least 35.

restaurant_chain_founded.question: Which restaurant chain is older?
restaurant_chain_founded.definition_note: Year the chain's first restaurant opened under its founders.
restaurant_chain_founded.fact_default: White Castle's first burgers cost five cents.

river_length.question: Which river is longer?
river_length.definition_note: Length of the main stem in kilometres. River lengths are disputed, so pairs closer than 10% are never used.
river_length.fact_default: River lengths depend on where you decide the source is, so estimates vary.

snack_launch_year.question: Which went on sale first?
snack_launch_year.question_low: Which went on sale more recently?
snack_launch_year.definition_note: Year the product first went on sale, under any name.
snack_launch_year.fact_default: Ketchup was sold as a medicine in the 1830s.

solar_body_diameter.question: Which is bigger across?
solar_body_diameter.definition_note: Mean diameter in kilometres (twice the volumetric mean radius), per NASA fact sheets.
solar_body_diameter.fact_default: Planets bulge at the equator, so their mean diameter is a little less than the equatorial one.

song_length.subject: song
song_length.question: Which song is longer?
song_length.definition_note: Length of the original album version (or the original single if it was not on an album).
song_length.fact_default: Most hit singles of the 1950s and '60s ran under three minutes, to fit radio and 45 rpm records.

song_release_year.subject: song
song_release_year.question: Which song came out first?
song_release_year.question_low: Which song came out more recently?
song_release_year.definition_note: Year of the recording's first commercial release, as a single or on an album, whichever came first.
song_release_year.fact_default: The Billboard Hot 100 chart began in August 1958.

tv_episode_count.question: Which TV series has more episodes?
tv_episode_count.question_low: Which TV series has fewer episodes?
tv_episode_count.definition_note: Total episodes of the original run, as counted by the series' official episode list. Revivals excluded.
tv_episode_count.fact_default: The Simpsons has aired more than 750 episodes.

us_city_population.subject: us_city
us_city_population.question: Which city had more people in the 2020 census?
us_city_population.question_low: Which city had fewer people in the 2020 census?
us_city_population.definition_note: Population of the city proper (not the metro area) counted by the 2020 US Census, April 1, 2020.
us_city_population.fact_default: These counts are for city limits only; metro areas are often several times larger.

us_state_area.subject: us_state
us_state_area.question: Which state is bigger?
us_state_area.definition_note: Total area (land plus water) in square miles, per the US Census Bureau.
us_state_area.fact_default: Alaska is bigger than Texas, California and Montana combined.

us_state_population.subject: us_state
us_state_population.question: Which state had more people in the 2020 census?
us_state_population.question_low: Which state had fewer people in the 2020 census?
us_state_population.definition_note: Resident population on April 1, 2020, from the 2020 US Census apportionment counts.
us_state_population.fact_default: The 2020 census counted 331,449,281 people in the United States.

x_weight.question: Which is heavier?
x_weight.scope_note: Adult body mass; Pokédex weight for Pokémon
x_weight.definition_note: Real animals: typical adult body mass (AnAge, PanTHERIA). Pokémon: official Pokédex weight (PokéAPI, Pokémon Showdown).
x_weight.fact_default: Pokédex weights are the official figures from the games.

x_lifetime.question: Which lasted longer?
x_lifetime.scope_note: Longest recorded lifespan; length of reign
x_lifetime.definition_note: Animals: longest recorded lifespan (AnAge, PanTHERIA). Monarchs: length of reign over England or Britain.
x_lifetime.fact_default: Queen Elizabeth II reigned for 70 years, the longest of any British monarch.

x_length.question: Which is longer?
x_length.definition_note: Coastlines from the CIA World Factbook; diameters of planets and moons from NASA.
x_length.fact_default: Coastline lengths depend on how closely you measure: the finer the ruler, the longer the coast.

x_height.question: Which is taller?
x_height.definition_note: Buildings: architectural height (CTBUH). Roller coasters: structure height (RCDB), converted from feet.
x_height.fact_default: Falcons Flight in Saudi Arabia, the tallest roller coaster, stands about 163 m.

x_area.question: Which is bigger?
x_area.definition_note: States: total area (US Census Bureau). National parks: area from the National Park Service, converted from acres.
x_area.fact_default: Wrangell–St. Elias, the biggest US national park, is larger than nine US states.

x_population.question: Which had more people in the 2020 census?
x_population.question_low: Which had fewer people in the 2020 census?
x_population.definition_note: 2020 US Census counts for cities and states.
x_population.fact_default: New York City has more people than 39 of the 50 US states.

abraham-lincoln.fact: Lincoln is the only US president to hold a patent.

albert-einstein.fact: Einstein was offered the presidency of Israel in 1952 and declined.

betty-white.fact: Betty White died 17 days before her 100th birthday.

charles-darwin.fact: Darwin and Abraham Lincoln were born on the same day: February 12, 1809.

charlie-chaplin.fact: Chaplin was knighted in 1975, two years before he died.

cleopatra.fact: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.

isaac-newton.fact: Newton also served as Warden and then Master of the Royal Mint.

jimmy-carter.fact: Jimmy Carter was the first US president to reach 100.

leonardo-da-vinci.fact: Leonardo wrote many of his notes in mirror writing.

ludwig-van-beethoven.fact: Beethoven wrote his Ninth Symphony while almost completely deaf.

marie-curie.fact: Marie Curie was the first person to win Nobel Prizes in two sciences.

mark-twain.fact: Mark Twain was born and died in years when Halley's Comet appeared.

martin-luther-king-jr.fact: King was 35 when he won the Nobel Peace Prize, then its youngest winner.

michelangelo.fact: Michelangelo was still working on sculptures days before he died.

napoleon-bonaparte.fact: Napoleon was about average height for his time; the "short" myth came from British cartoons.

nelson-mandela.fact: Mandela spent 27 years in prison before becoming South Africa's president.

pablo-picasso.fact: Picasso made an estimated 50,000 works of art.

queen-elizabeth-ii.fact: Elizabeth II reigned for 70 years, longer than any other British monarch.

stephen-hawking.fact: Stephen Hawking died on Albert Einstein's birthday, March 14.

thomas-jefferson.fact: Jefferson died on July 4, 1826, the 50th anniversary of the Declaration, the same day as John Adams.

vincent-van-gogh.fact: Van Gogh sold very few paintings during his lifetime.

winston-churchill.fact: Churchill won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1953.

burj-al-arab.fact: Burj Al Arab stands on its own artificial island.

burj-khalifa.fact: Burj Khalifa has been the world's tallest building since 2010.
